paper.title_en: Demographics of Off-Nuclear Tidal Disruption Events Powered by Wandering Black Holes
paper.abstract_en: The four recently discovered off-nuclear tidal disruption events (TDEs)---EP240222a, AT2024tvd, AT2025abcr, and AT2023mfm---together with those found serendipitously over past decades (ESO 243-49 HLX-1 and 3XMM J2150-05), reveal a small but robust population of accreting off-nuclear, or ``wandering'' black holes (WBHs). We analyze their demographic properties in comparison to other populations, we find that (i) every event occurs in a massive early-type galaxy within the narrow range $10.7 \lesssim \log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot) \lesssim 11.1$, a range that very rarely hosts nuclear TDEs; (ii) their radial displacements span $1 \lesssim R_{\bullet}/{\rm kpc} \lesssim 40$, or $0.003 \lesssim R_{\bullet}/R_{200} \lesssim 0.1$; (iii) a stellar counterpart is detected in pre-TDE observations only when located outside the galaxy's half-light radius; (iv) while nuclear TDE hosts are usually isolated, off-nuclear TDEs and quiescent WBHs are more likely to inhabit galaxy groups or clusters. Using the \texttt{ROMULUS} cosmological simulation, we show that all of these follow naturally from hierarchical galaxy formation. We construct the volumetric density of WBHs, $φ_{\rm WBH}(M_{\star})$, which places the central 68\% of local WBHs in galaxies with $10.7 \lesssim \log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot) \lesssim 11.3$, explaining (i) and (iv). This WBH distribution can imply a higher off-nuclear than nuclear TDE rate, at these galaxy masses. Their intrinsic radial distribution is Gaussian-like in $\log_{10}(R_\bullet/R_{200})$, consistent with (ii) except for a deficit of sources at the largest separations. Combined with parent-galaxy light, which suppresses counterpart detections at small separations, this distribution also explains (iii). These results show that off-nuclear TDEs are the accreting counterparts of the WBHs long predicted by cosmological simulations, and that they trace large-scale structure.
